title: Pathwarden finding action: request (pathwarden.action-request.v1)
description: What Pathwarden writes to a finding action program's stdin: a describe request (what do you offer?) or a run request (run this action on this finding). PATHWARDEN_ACTION_REQUEST names the kind too. docs/actions.md explains each field. Within v1 fields are only added: a program must ignore fields it doesn't know, so the schema allows them.

settings.description: The [[action]] block's keys other than name, plugin, command, timeout_seconds, min_severity, rules and categories, as TOML gave them (text, numbers, true or false, lists, tables). A secret is never here: a setting whose name ends in _env names an environment variable, and that variable is in the program's environment.

action.description: The id of the action to run, from the program's describe. Empty only in `pathwarden action request`'s output when no action is set up.

inputs.description: Every input the action describes, by id, already checked: text (trimmed; a textarea's line breaks as \n) for text, textarea and choice inputs (a choice exactly as described), true or false for bool. An input left empty is "", or its default.

dry_run.description: True: the program must change nothing. It may read, and should check everything it can short of changing something.

run_id.description: The run the finding is in, e.g. 20261118T140200.000Z.

pathwarden.description: The Pathwarden version that analyzed the run.

record.description: For a follow-up (an action with for: "record"), the record it runs on, as saved on the finding; else null.

by.description: Who asked: the user, e.g. SCALE\analyst. Null when unknown.

on.description: The computer they asked from. Null when unknown.

finding.description: The finding as the run's event document (pathwarden.event.v1, docs/dev/formats.md) has it, plus guide and status. An open or accepted finding has every field of the event's findings; a fixed one only those of resolved (fingerprint, rule, severity, first_seen, resolved_at, title), a held one only those of held (fingerprint, rule).

fingerprint.description: The finding's ID, e.g. PW-006-1bbba15126c6fc31. It stays the same across runs: use it as the key in the other system.

status.description: Where the finding stands in the run.

guide.description: The rule's step-by-step guide, in Markdown, or null.

suppressed.description: The accepted risk's reason, or null.

accepted.description: Who accepted the risk, when, its review date and notes.

resolved_at.description: A fixed finding: when it was gone, in Unix seconds.

record.description: A record kept on the finding: what a result returned (id, kind, label, number, url, status, open, fields), and which action made it, who first ran it, where and when, and when it last changed.

action.description: The action that made it, as <block name>/<id>.
